abstract: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) remodeling contributing to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. This study aimed to identify clinically relevant mitochondrial OXPHOS-associated biomarkers and evaluate their biological, immunological, and prognostic significance in non-small cell lung cancer. Publicly available transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical datasets were integrated to identify differentially expressed OXPHOS-related genes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC). Functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction, gene co-expression, pathway, immune infiltration, mutation, expression, and survival analyses were performed using established bioinformatics approaches. An eight-gene mitochondrial OXPHOS-centered network comprising COX6B1, COX5B, NDUFS8, NDUFB10, NDUFA12, NDUFB11, ECSIT, and TXN2 was identified. These genes were primarily associated with respiratory electron transport, oxidative phosphorylation, ATP metabolism, mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes, and electron transfer. Immune analyses revealed associations between OXPHOS alterations and immune-cell infiltration in LUAD and LUSC. Elevated expressions of COX6B1, COX5B, NDUFS8, NDUFA12, NDUFB11, and ECSIT was associated with poorer overall survival, whereas TXN2 showed no significant prognostic association. These findings identify a mitochondrial OXPHOS-related gene signature with potential prognostic and therapeutic relevance in lung cancer.
